title: Scaling Multiagent Systems with Process Rewards
relevance_note: Topology-aware multiagent training source grounded in terminal environments and explicit specialization.
reason_included: Defines pre-set multiagent topologies in terminal settings and reports architecture-linked training effects.

claim_snippets.claim_text: On held-out tasks, MAPPA reports gains of +5.0 to +17.5 points on AIME/AMC and +12.5 points success-rate improvement on DSBench; its own analysis also finds coach-score bias can induce unwanted specialization.
MAPPA uses a coach model to assign per-action process rewards based on role, observed context, action, and tool feedback, addressing inter-agent credit assignment that sparse outcome rewards miss.

MAPPA trains tool-augmented multiagent systems in a terminal environment where agents with separate weights execute in a pre-defined topology such as sequential pipeline, debate, or mixture-of-agents.
